name: Fosfomycin
route_note: Single oral sachet of fosfomycin trometamol for cystitis; IV fosfomycin disodium (outside the US) for systemic infections in combination.
originator: Merck & Co. and Compañía Española de Penicilina y Antibióticos (CEPA)

discovery.note: Discovered in Streptomyces fradiae isolated from a Spanish soil sample; now produced synthetically.

tagline: Single-dose oral treatment for cystitis and an IV option for resistant bacteria
summary: Fosfomycin is a small phosphonic acid antibiotic discovered in 1969 that blocks the first committed step of peptidoglycan synthesis. Oral fosfomycin trometamol is given as a single dose for uncomplicated cystitis, and intravenous fosfomycin is used, usually in combination, for multidrug-resistant infections in Europe and elsewhere.
mechanism: Fosfomycin enters bacteria via the glycerol-3-phosphate (GlpT) and hexose-phosphate (UhpT) transporters and covalently alkylates the active-site cysteine of MurA, preventing formation of UDP-N-acetylmuramic acid and thus the earliest cytoplasmic step of cell-wall synthesis.

Because its target is unique, there is no cross-resistance with other classes. Resistance arises readily in vitro through transporter mutations, and plasmid-borne fos enzymes (FosA, FosB, FosX) inactivate it, which is why IV use is combined with other agents.
uses: Lower UTI caused by ESBL-producing E. coli
Combination therapy of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative and staphylococcal infections (IV)
Prophylaxis for transrectal prostate biopsy (some countries)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Fosfomycin is reported by Merck and CEPA scientists in Science.

history.title: US oral approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Monurol (fosfomycin trometamol) for uncomplicated UTI in women.

history.title: WHO AWaRe classification
history.detail: WHO begins grouping antibiotics on its Essential Medicines List into Access, Watch and Reserve; intravenous fosfomycin is a Reserve antibiotic.

history.title: ZEUS trial and US IV application
history.detail: The ZEUS trial supports IV fosfomycin (Contepo) for complicated UTI, but the FDA issues a complete response letter citing manufacturing issues.

history.title: EMA review
history.detail: The EMA recommends that oral fosfomycin trometamol be restricted to uncomplicated cystitis and some prophylaxis and that IV use be reserved for serious infections when other antibiotics are unsuitable.

pk.half_life: about 2–4 hours (oral trometamol up to about 5–6 hours)
pk.excretion: renal, unchanged, giving high and prolonged urinary concentrations

serious: Hypokalaemia and sodium overload with IV fosfomycin disodium

facts: Fosfomycin is one of the smallest antibiotics in clinical use, with a molecular mass of about 138 Da for the free acid.
